title: Feature: Global workspace sync for multi-monitor setups
head: e0c507e9ac07
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Live-monitor filter silently skips every target when enumeration succeeds but no saved monitor name matches; on enumeration error it restores the disconnected-monitor bug
leads.consequence: With stale saved names during connector changes or a monitor snapshot with no matches, SUPER+N dispatches nothing and exits successfully. Conversely a failed or malformed `hyprctl monitors -j` falls back to all saved bases and creates/focuses workspaces for disconnected monitors. No warning distinguishes either case. Next successful sync may recover the first case, while repeat enumeration failures keep the second case.
leads.triage: partly corroborated (Opus F3a: empty-list no-dispatch and fallback); judged unreachable in normal sessions; not published

leads.summary: The global-switch test never exercises the new successful-JSON connected-monitor filter
leads.consequence: Every test stub for `hyprctl monitors -j` either prints a shell log line or empty stdout, so the new parser throws and executes its fallback branch. Tests for the disconnected-monitor fix pass even if the filter is removed entirely. Add a real monitors JSON response and assert that an unplugged saved base never gets a workspace dispatch; test empty/unmatched and command-failure cases separately.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus M2; published as optional test note

leads.summary: A delayed workspace materializer can run after global mode is disabled
leads.consequence: The helper sleeps one second, gates on a persistent bases file and Hyprland session but never rechecks the toggle flag. If the user disables global mode or reloads during that second, it dispatches to every missing global ID on still-connected monitors under local mode and attempts to restore an old active ID. On the next reload the saved bases remain, so another outstanding job can repeat the action. Check the current toggle after sleeping and before each batch.
leads.triage: behavioural, pre-existing in PR, not affected by new commit; low value; dropped

leads.summary: The added ALT-binding assertions pass when all ALT bindings are deleted
leads.consequence: Removing all ten SUPER+SHIFT+ALT+N bindings is a plausible binding edit that would remove silent move for users, but both `while` loops iterate zero rows, print PASS and never fail. Assert exactly ten SILENT_MOVE and ten FOLLOW_MOVE records before validating their --silent values.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus M1 (mutant m4); published as optional test note

leads.summary: Custom XDG_STATE_HOME can put the loaded toggle in a different location from the feature's CLI, bar and helper state
leads.consequence: Omarchy's Lua loader honors XDG_STATE_HOME, while omarchy-hyprland-toggle writes `$HOME/.local/state`, as do the new wrappers, monitor base store and bar probe. If a user moves a flag into the custom state directory to enable it, Lua synchronizes displays while SUPER+N takes the local path; if they run the CLI to enable it, wrappers/bar say global but Lua does not load. Restore a common state-path contract or document/migrate it.
leads.triage: XDG_STATE_HOME split; toggle-path convention is base Omarchy (omarchy-hyprland-toggle uses HOME path); out of scope; dropped

leads.summary: Bar maps a workspace outside all assigned monitor ranges to a slot that the Lua synchronizer ignores
leads.consequence: With saved bases 0,10 and 20, navigating to an unrelated workspace ID 42 makes the bar mark slot 2 and its windows as occupied, yet `slot_of(42)` returns nil and the other displays stay unsynced. Clicking the indicated slot 2 then switches to IDs 2/12/22 instead of 42. Determine bar slot membership from the saved base ranges, not merely a modulo and an upper bound.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus M3 (cosmetic bar mismatch); not published

leads.summary: Related PR #11935's opt-in replaces the global workspace bindings rather than composing with them
leads.consequence: If both modes are enabled after reconciling the one conflict region, #11935's selected branch sends SUPER+N directly to the current monitor and bypasses the global-switch helper; the Lua hook may still synchronize after an active event but there is no guaranteed global helper path. If the merge instead keeps #12978's entire loop, #11935's opt-in silently does nothing. Define how the two opt-ins compose, and test the merged bindings under both flags before shipping.
leads.triage: conditional conflict with open PR #11935; not verified as merged conflict impact; dropped

leads.summary: Re-running tester installer destroys the original bar widget backup
leads.consequence: The script labels all steps idempotent at line 10 but every repeat run copies the current installed widget over `Workspaces.qml.bak`. After two runs, the documented restore command at line 168 restores the PR widget rather than the original; the tester cannot undo the overwrite from that backup. Skip copying if backup exists or use a distinct per-run backup; do not run this script in the normal install flow.
leads.triage: factual, verified tools/install.sh:10,119-128,167-168 by coordinator and Opus; published under F4

leads.summary: The new opt-in mode is not discoverable in the user manual
leads.consequence: The shipping manual still explains only local workspace moves and bar clicks, without how to enable or disable global sync or what slot numbers mean on a second monitor. The only enable instructions in this patch are in the tester-only tools/install.sh. Add an opt-in section to the workspace navigation manual and update the bar row for global mode.

leads.summary: Related PR #13369's bar model omits this PR's IDs 11-20 and above
leads.consequence: If #13369's model is used unchanged in a combined resolution, it discards every workspace rule for ID>10, while this PR registers IDs 11-20 for monitor 2. Because at least monitor 1 has 1-10 rules, bound mode is true, the second monitor's bar has no rule IDs and filters all its actual >10 workspaces, leaving an empty bar. The conflicts prevent automatic merge: adapt the model to per-monitor base ranges and logical slots instead of applying its widget hunk unchanged.
leads.triage: conditional conflict with open PR #13369; dropped

leads.summary: Existing enabled state copies remain on the previous toggle code after a source upgrade
leads.consequence: A tester who enabled global mode on the previous head has a copied workspace-global.lua under state. Updating the PR tree to e0c507e9 and reloading loads that older copy, so the new refocus and dynamic range fixes never run, although bin wrappers are updated. `omarchy-refresh-hyprland` only copies flags.lua. Re-enable the toggle to recopy it, or add an explicit migration for an already-enabled flag if supporting PR testers/early adopters.
leads.triage: verified bin/omarchy-hyprland-toggle copies on 'on' only; base toggle design, not introduced by PR; dropped

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on [the previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5822384452) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5823291434), checked at `e0c507e9ac07`.

**Outcome:** the new commit resolves the previous review's functional findings and its optional test note. The tester installer cleanup item is still present (moved to `tools/install.sh`), and one new test regression was found. A SUPER+CTRL+TAB focus problem, previously listed under the focus finding, has a separate, pre-existing cause and remains (modelled from source, see below).

**Verified:** SUPER+SHIFT+N follows again in local mode, the switch helper skips disconnected monitors, and hotplugged high-base monitors sync without a reload. The Lua hook keeps focus on the current monitor for SUPER+TAB, SUPER+SHIFT+TAB and scroll (source-derived, with SUPER+TAB also modelled; not a native run). The suggested test assertions were added.

**Still open:** an older test contradicts the new SUPER+SHIFT+N behavior, so `./test/shell` now reports a failure. The tester installer was moved and relabelled but still ships with the PR.

| Previous finding | Status at `e0c507e9ac07` |
|---|---|
| SUPER+SHIFT+N no longer follows the window in local mode | **Resolved** |
| Lua hook moves focus off the current monitor | **Resolved** for SUPER+TAB, SUPER+SHIFT+TAB and scroll. Source-derived (SUPER+TAB also modelled), not a native run. SUPER+CTRL+TAB has a separate cause (see below) |
| Switch helper iterates disconnected monitors | **Resolved** |
| Lua `ws_id_upper_bound` stale after hotplug | **Resolved** |
| Root `install.sh` tester installer | **Still present** as `tools/install.sh` (see below) |
| Optional test: assert local-mode follow and silent dispatch | **Resolved.** The new assertions fail against `ab8e77e0cfd7` and pass here |

**Verified details:**
- **Follow and silent moves:** SUPER+SHIFT+ALT+N now passes `--silent`. Without it, the wrapper's local-mode branch dispatches `hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = "N" })`, the same form the base bound directly. In Hyprland 0.56.2 a move without `follow` switches to the target workspace with the window (`LuaBindingsDispatchers.cpp`, `ConfigActions.cpp` `moveToWorkspace`).
- **Refocus in the hook:** `hl.dsp.focus({ monitor = name })` exists in 0.56.2, matches the monitor by name, does nothing when that monitor already has focus, and never changes workspace. Hyprland does not re-enter a running `hl.on` handler, so the hook's own dispatches cannot loop. In a Lua model of these rules, SUPER+TAB now leaves focus on the originating monitor with two and three monitors.
- **Live-monitor filter:** against a stub `hyprctl` with one saved but disconnected monitor, the switch helper now dispatches only to connected monitors (`12, 2`). When the `monitors -j` query fails it falls back to all saved bases (`12, 22, 2`), which is what `ab8e77e0cfd7` did in every case.
- **Hotplug bound:** `slot_of` now checks the current bases table (refreshed on hotplug) on every call. In the model, a hotplugged monitor with base 90 syncs slot 10 at this head and not at `ab8e77e0cfd7`.

## New in this revision

### `move-window-to-aw-test.sh` now fails

[`move-window-to-aw-test.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/e0c507e9ac074e25b26730c1a2a11de55f933d44/test/shell.d/move-window-to-aw-test.sh#L58-L65) was not updated. It still calls `omarchy-move-window-to-aw 3` without `--silent` and expects `follow = false`, which the new follow behavior intentionally omits:

```text
got: hyprctl dispatch hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = "3" })
not ok - local mode passes follow=false for silent move
```

**Impact:** `./test/shell` fails at this head. In isolated full-suite runs of the shell tests, this file is the only difference between `ab8e77e0cfd7` and this head; the other failures appear at both commits, in files this PR does not touch, and are mostly missing sandbox prerequisites. The new assertions in `workspace-global-bindings-test.sh` expect the opposite result for the same call without `--silent`, so the two files contradict each other.

**Suggested change:** call it with `--silent 3` in that check, or assert both forms there and drop the duplicate from the bindings test.

## Still present

### Tester installer still ships as `tools/install.sh`

The script moved to a new top-level `tools/` directory with a "NOT part of Omarchy's install or update path" header. It still uses `sudo` to overwrite files under `/usr/share/omarchy`, copies helpers into `~/.local/bin` and appends a PATH line to `~/.bashrc`/`~/.zshrc`.

**Impact:** a merge would add a pre-merge tester script to the repository. The script is also out of date:
- Its header still lists files "matching PR caff3e03".
- It does not install `default/hypr/bindings/tiling.lua`, so testers do not get the new bindings, despite "This mirrors what the PR adds".
- A second run copies the already-replaced bar widget over `Workspaces.qml.bak`, losing the original the script later tells users to restore, despite "Safe to re-run".

**Suggested change:** keep it out of the tree, for example in a gist or the PR description.

## Pre-existing: SUPER+CTRL+TAB in global mode (modelled, not a native run)

This was listed under the focus finding in the previous review, but it has a separate cause that the refocus does not address. SUPER+CTRL+TAB is bound to `focus({ workspace = "previous" })`, which uses Hyprland's global workspace history. The hook's own switches are recorded there too (`WorkspaceHistoryTracker.cpp`). After a synced switch from slot 3 to slot 4, "previous" resolves to slot 4 on the other monitor.

**Impact:** in the model, SUPER+CTRL+TAB in global mode moves focus to the other monitor with no slot change instead of returning to the former slot. This happens both at `ab8e77e0cfd7` and at this head, so it is not caused by the new commit. It is source-derived and needs a live two-monitor check.

**Suggested change (untested):** in global mode, bind SUPER+CTRL+TAB to `previous_per_monitor`, which limits the lookup to the focused monitor.

## Optional test improvements

- Section 1b of `workspace-global-bindings-test.sh` has no count check. A mutant that reorders the silent binding's modifiers and drops `--silent` passes the whole file, because the loop then matches nothing. A count check like section 1's would catch that.
- The `hyprctl` stub in `workspace-global-switch-test.sh` returns nothing for `monitors -j`, so the new live-monitor filter only ever runs its fallback. Returning monitor JSON from the stub would cover it.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** pinned-source inspection of `e0c507e9ac07` against `ab8e77e0cfd7` and the base, with Hyprland 0.56.2 source (the key focus, dispatcher and event-guard functions behave the same on current `main`). Isolated command runs covered the full `./test/shell` and `./test/cli` suites at head and `ab8e77e0cfd7`, the new assertions against `ab8e77e0cfd7` code and targeted mutants, the switch helper against a stub `hyprctl`, and a Lua model of the hook's focus, hotplug and history behavior. No native Hyprland, multi-monitor, hotplug or keybinding test was run, and `tools/install.sh` was not executed. Focus, hotplug and SUPER+CTRL+TAB results are source-derived or modelled.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
